docs/figures/the-monitor-reads-each-fact.data_ink: pass — the ink is two flat grey bar series, their numeric labels and two short annotations; no gradient, shadow, hatch or filled band is present, and the only decoration is a frameless legend in empty upper-right space.
docs/figures/the-monitor-reads-each-fact.decoration: pass — no gridlines, no background shading or band, and the top and right spines are absent, leaving the left scale and the bottom axis as the only rules; measured on the PNG the top-right quadrant between the legend and the third group is blank white.

docs/figures/the-monitor-reads-each-fact.legibility: pass — three labelled rounds read at a glance: cold 81 KiB tick against 238 KiB sweep pass, unchanged zero for both with 'nothing changed: no bytes read' above them, and the rewritten-plan round 4 KiB tick with 884 B sweep pass, annotated 'extension of the bytes that arrived' and 'one plan re-read'. findings.disposition_reason: The linear axis is required by the two exact-zero rows the figure exists to show, and both third-round values are stated directly above their bars in their own units, so the smallest bars are read from their labels without ambiguity.
findings.summary: On the linear 0-238 KiB axis the third round's bars are near-invisible: the 884 B sweep-pass bar renders as a single row of pixels at the baseline and the 4 KiB tick bar as about nine rows, so that round's two magnitudes are read from the labelled numbers rather than from bar height. The scale is honest — two exact zeros in the same figure rule out a log axis — and both values are printed above the bars, so the datum is not lost.

findings.disposition_reason: The two neutral fills still separate tick from sweep pass in this render and every bar carries its own value above it, so the datum is legible without the fill; moving the sweep-pass fill to a feature colour is a palette decision for the figure family, owned by the style module that sets the figure-wide colours, not a defect in this figure.
findings.summary: The sweep-pass bars are filled #bdbdbd against the tick's #929292. The figure's headline datum (238 KiB) therefore sits in the palest mark on the page: at roughly 1.6:1 against white it is lighter than the #b0b0b0 that this project's figure guidance already rejected as fading out, and the two compared series are told apart by lightness alone rather than by one feature colour against a neutral. It reads on screen at this size, but it will wash out on a projector or a pale print.

findings.disposition_reason: The annotation states its meaning in words directly above the bar it names, so the blue is emphasis rather than an encoding a reader must decode; no series is confused by it.
findings.summary: The muted blue (#2b6cb0) is used for exactly one annotation, 'extension of the bytes that arrived', and appears in no legend entry, so nothing on the page tells a reader what blue signifies — it reads as an unexplained emphasis rather than as a third series. The sentence itself is clear and is written in the bar's colour role, so no reader is misled; the only cost is an unresolved colour.
